sampling_model.design: A triangular array of binary sequential experiments with fixed finite-population potential outcomes and assignment as the only randomness.
sampling_model.treatment: Given \(\mathcal F_{n,t-1}\), \(A_{nt}\) is Bernoulli with known logged predictable probability \(e_{nt}\).
sampling_model.overlap: The rare-arm probability follows \(t e_{nt}\approx \bar q(t/n)\) after an early cutoff, with bounded cumulative hazard and \(0<e_{nt}\le\rho<1\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Predictable regressions \(m_{nt}(a)\) may be arbitrary within their bound; their treated residuals follow a deterministic Lipschitz profile on one common high-probability event.
sampling_model.randomness: Only the known adaptive randomization law is random; there is no superpopulation sampling assumption.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Definition 1 permits general positive history-dependent assignment probabilities, while Theorem 4(ii)'s Gaussian AIPW conclusion requires Condition 3, including its negligible-maximum part (ii).
Theorem 1 constructs doubly robust betting confidence sequences under predictable logging.
Proposition 1 proves selective type-I error control for the selective randomization p-value.
Theorem 1 proves asymptotic type-I error control for simulation with optimism in specified adaptive designs.
Proposition 2 gives an exact compound-Poisson law for an HT rate estimator under independent Poisson importance sampling.
Finite-population limited-overlap estimators are asymptotically Gaussian when their effective sample size diverges.
Any valid i.i.d. bounded-mean confidence interval obeys an inverse-information-projection width lower bound.
Stein perturbation yields explicit total-variation compound-Poisson approximation bounds for integer-valued sums.
Weighted Bernoulli and Poisson sums admit generalized Dickman approximation bounds.
Theorem 1 gives a semiparametrically efficient Gaussian limit for the truncated A2IPW estimator.
Resampling simulations find tighter superior-arm and wider inferior-arm intervals under real-time adaptive randomization.

body.tldr: At the critical rare-arm boundary, where cumulative allocation hazard stays bounded, the finite-population AIPW error need not be Gaussian. On this note's structured binary profile subclass, a stopped adaptive-to-Bernoulli-to-Poisson transfer and directed-rational convolution give a computable atom-safe confidence interval with uniform randomization coverage and explicit oracle level and radius slack. Separately, the parameterized late-ramp family with intensity \(c/t\), ramp start \(a_\star\), and amplitude \(\delta\) proves an all-confidence-set frontier: asymptotic \((1-\alpha)\)-honesty on both signs forces diameter at least \(\delta(1-a_\star)\) with limiting probability at least \(a_\star^c-2\alpha\). These witnesses belong to Li and Zhao's larger baseline binary adaptive class but fail their Gaussian Condition 3(ii), so only the converse transfers to that class. The exact \(c=a_\star=1/2\), \(\delta=1/4\), \(\alpha=0.05\) corollary preserves the \(1/8\) diameter and \(0.60710678\) probability, while the declared high-hazard subfamily retains robust radius at most \(0.442M\) apart from certification slack.

project_justification.gap: Li and Zhao's baseline design class permits positive history-dependent adaptive probabilities and their AIPW theorem gives Gaussian inference only under Condition 3; it does not characterize honest-set width when the negligible-maximum condition fails at bounded cumulative hazard. Existing anytime-valid or i.i.d. width results likewise do not calibrate the signed atomic compound-Poisson law or exploit a shared complete-log void event.
project_justification.niche: The bounded-hazard boundary has two linked but distinct phenomena. Structured deterministic profiles make atom-safe positive calibration computationally possible, whereas a parameterized two-sign late ramp creates a common observational subprobability component of limiting mass \(a_\star^c\) on the void event and a causal separation \(\delta(1-a_\star)\), yielding an estimator-free width obstruction.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies a computable finite adaptive-to-Poisson transfer and profile-net interval theorem on the declared structured subclass, together with a parameterized probability--diameter frontier for arbitrary complete-log confidence sets. A sourced subclass-inclusion argument lifts that converse, but not the positive calibration theorem, to Li and Zhao's broader baseline binary adaptive-design class; the exact ramp and high-hazard numerical certificates remain preserved diagnostics.

body.related_work: Li and Zhao (2026) provide the closest design-based setup: fixed finite-population potential outcomes, positive assignment probabilities that may be arbitrary prespecified functions of history, and predictable AIPW regression. Their Definition 1 and Sections 2.2--2.3 contain the parameterized late ramps as binary special cases, but their Theorem 4(ii) assumes Condition 3; the ramps fail part (ii) because their standardized late increments remain nonnegligible. The present parameterized frontier therefore transfers by subclass inclusion to their baseline class, while the positive profile-net calibration remains confined to this note's structured binary profile subclass. Bibaut and Kallus (2024) organize adaptive inference into martingale-CLT repair, always-valid methods, and direct inversion of nonnormal laws; their review identifies the last route as incomplete beyond special settings. Waudby-Smith et al. (2024) provide exact predictable-logging martingale confidence sequences but do not determine the signed atomic profile radius. Freidling, Zhao, and Gao (2026) condition exact randomization tests on adaptive selection, whereas the present same-log calibration uses deterministic threshold domination. Cho, Bibaut, and Kallus (2025) invert simulated nonnormal adaptive laws under stochastic bandit models; here the inference is finite-population and certification errors are directed outward. Chen et al. (2026) derive a compound-Poisson HT rate law under independent Poisson importance sampling, not a signed adaptive causal contrast with uniform finite-experiment transfer. Hong, Leung, and Li (2020) study limited overlap when effective information diverges, and Shekhar and Ramdas (2023) prove i.i.d. bounded-mean width bounds rather than a common-subprobability frontier for a complete sequential experiment. Barbour and Xia (1999) motivate explicit compound-Poisson error accounting, while Bhattacharjee and Goldstein (2019) identify the generalized Dickman constant-profile reduction. Liberali et al. (2025) remain the applied consumer, conditional on a prespecified expected-endpoint bridge for their GUSTO-1 and EUROPA adaptive-randomization analysis.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The finite-transfer theorem couples the AIPW statistic, not the complete statistical experiments, and therefore cannot imply the all-estimator lower bound. The parameterized diameter frontier instead uses a separate common-subprobability argument on the exact late-arm void event. The late ramps lie in Li and Zhao's baseline adaptive class but violate their Gaussian Condition 3(ii); this supports transfer of the converse only and does not extend the positive calibration result beyond the declared deterministic-profile subclass. Profiles must be fixed before the path is realized, same-log threshold selection requires deterministic domination, and exact no-slack quantile convergence is not asserted at atoms. The high-hazard \(0.442M\) result is an upper bound on a declared subfamily, not a globally sharp minimax-width constant.
body.honest_scope: The positive result covers the declared bounded Lipschitz intensity and signed-residual profile subclass with a supplied common profile event, early quadratic-variation envelope, and certified inputs. It does not cover Li and Zhao's full baseline adaptive class. The converse is broader: the parameterized late ramps form a subclass of that baseline class, so uniform honesty there inherits the bound \(a_\star^c-2\alpha\) at diameter \(\delta(1-a_\star)\), nontrivially when \(a_\star^c>2\alpha\). The exact \(16\)-bin ramp computation, the \(0.60710678\) specialization, and the high-hazard \(0.442M\) arithmetic are reproducible diagnostics, not substitutes for the uniform positive theorem. The open polynomial-certificate question remains open with its existing pruning-complexity obstruction; no bit-complexity exponent is asserted. The Liberali et al. application is conditional on a prespecified expected-endpoint bridge that verifies the deterministic profile and modulus contract. Random-profile or Cox-process extensions, atom-free quantile claims, and globally optimal expected-width constants remain outside scope.
